Omdia today published a new research report detailing Apple's rumored roadmap for Mac and iPad over the coming years, and also mentioned that a much-rumored major product has been cancelled. Here are the details.

The foldable iPad/Mac hybrid that was once described by John Ternus as a 'priority project' is reported to have been cancelled

For years there have been rumors that the iPhone is only the first product line in which Apple will adopt a foldable display.

Reports have indicated that a larger, around 18 to 20-inch foldable iPad/Mac hybrid has been in development for years. Earlier rumors suggested it might launch in 2026, but it was subsequently pushed back to 2028.

Earlier this year, Mark Gurman referred to this product as the 'Ternus priority project,' but also hinted that it might never launch. He wrote:

You can find a detailed roundup of past rumors about this product here.

Based on Omdia's report today, Gurman's speculation may well be correct. The report states: 'The product plan for a 16.1-inch to 18-inch foldable MacBook has been cancelled.'

Based on previous rumors, this appears to be the same product that Gurman and others had previously reported on.

Top comment from Jay Diamond

In terms of pricing, this product would most likely belong to a high-end niche market (similar to the Vision Pro).

Especially given how ridiculously expensive chips have become these days.

So sales would be very limited.

It's quite possible that Apple is taking a 'wait-and-see' approach with this foldable product, waiting to see how the market responds to the foldable iPhone Ultra. If the iPhone Ultra sells well, the company may accelerate development of the iPad/MacBook hybrid.

However, possibly because the current memory crisis has already driven product prices up significantly, Apple may not see a way to launch such an ultra-premium, innovative foldable device at this moment.

What do you think about the rumored cancellation of the foldable iPad/MacBook? Let us know in the comments section.
